Devon (Customer): hi, hitting lots of 429s this morning in prod (eu-west-1). started ~2024-11-03T09:12Z. our dashboards show brief RPM spikes but most requests are legit user traffic. sample request-id: req_0a9c3f. headers show X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Limit: 600, Retry-After: 2
Marta (Support): thanks Devon — can you paste the exact timestamp window (UTC) and whether this is on Hosted or Dedicated for you? also any recent deploys?
Devon (Customer): hosted. window 09:12:20 - 09:14:10 UTC. no deploys. traffic pattern looks like 3 short bursts ~30s each, ~250 RPM peak per tenant, average 40 RPM.
Alex (SRE): initial thought: tenant's token-bucket exhausted due to bursty fanout from their cron jobs + many concurrent client connections. can you share sample client headers (keepalive, connection type) and whether using streaming?
Devon (Customer): they use short streaming sessions for typing indicators, roughly 50 concurrent streams across many endpoints. sample header we grabbed: 

  Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...
  Connection: keep-alive
  Accept: application/json
  X-Customer-Org: org_53

Marta (Support): ok, next steps for triage: 1) we need exact request IDs and logs for the 09:12-09:14 window (send to support-uploads). 2) we'll pull per-tenant throttle metrics (rpm/tpm and burst token consumption) and minute-aligned buckets. 3) please run a short repro if possible: a low-impact concurrency test.
Jin (Platform): tip: many clients open continuous short streams and occasionally re-open which can amplify token consumption if each stream refreshes auth or triggers prefixed prompts. if they do minute-aligned cron fanout + streaming reconnects you get refill stampede. long-term: add jitter to scheduled jobs and prefer a single broadcast connection.
Marta (Support): Devon — here's a quick repro you can run from your environment (non-prod first):

  # simple concurrency spike using hey
  hey -c 30 -n 600 -z 30s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

  watch the 429s and capture one request-id to share.

Devon (Customer): I can run that in 15m. we want a hotfix too — customers are affected. any short-term mitigation?
Alex (SRE): short-term options: 1) temporary per-tenant burst increase (safest fast option), 2) enable per-tenant smoothing policy (rate limiter smooths short spikes over a few minutes), 3) route to a less-congested region or Dedicated pool if on plan. I can apply a temporary burst bump for org_53 for 2 hours while we triage.
Marta (Support): please confirm you'd like the temporary bump, Devon. if yes we'll do it and monitor. also please send the logs after running the hey test.
Devon (Customer): please bump now, thanks.
Alex (SRE): doing the bump now — applying +10 burst tokens and raising short-window allowance from 600 -> 1200 for 2 hours. I'll monitor error rate and token fill graph.
Alex (SRE): quick observation from metrics: per-route token consumption spiked on /v1/generate and /v1/chat/completions; many connections closed and re-opened within <10s. looks like their client retries are aggressive.
Jin (Platform): recommend they implement exponential backoff with jitter; respect Retry-After header; and move heavy background jobs to staggered schedules. for streaming, avoid frequent reconnects — reuse sessions or multiplex.
Marta (Support): action items:
- Devon to run the hey repro and upload request-id/logs to support-uploads (assigned)
- Alex to monitor the temporary bump and rollback after 2h (in progress)
- Jin to add docs link for client-side best practices and a short checklist we can share

oncall-bot: quota-change: automated change applied to tenant org_53 by Alex (SRE) at 2024-11-03T09:19:05Z — +10 burst tokens, short-window allowance increased.

Devon (Customer): thanks team — will run the test and get logs. appreciate the quick bump.
Marta (Support): thanks Devon. follow up once you have the logs. we'll update thread with rollback time and any further changes. :thumbsup:
